analysis:
The supplied units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 628-1013) and only documentation. The patch adds a v0.10.13 candidate header and highlights, with no source, configuration or workflow code changed in the visible evidence. I read the retained historical release-note text for security-relevant claims: the prefix-cache early-terminal opt-in (lines 651-669), tool_choice auto behavior (671-676), the watchdog rollback and restart handling (678-687), the local-API/me-first pair behavior, the CI watchdog workflow and the sandbox sizing. These entries are descriptive, and no code in this batch demonstrates a regression.

Relevant threat IDs for later passes. T-041 covers the prefix cache; the opt-in DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_TERMINAL_BEFORE_PUBLICATION is default off and keeps capacity held until the write settles. It changes timing and write ordering but not the HMAC, TTL or KEK posture, so no new at-rest exposure is shown here. T-043 and TB-003 cover the watchdog; the stop-record logic that distinguishes requested restarts from failed starts is described in prose only. The actual implementation should be reviewed to confirm that a crash or kill is still timed from the update launch, and that the stop record cannot be forged by a same-UID process to evade rollback. This cannot be judged from the changelog. T-053/T-054 are unaffected. TB-007/T-008 relate to the tool_choice auto relaxation. Returning undeclared tool names and schema-mismatched arguments unvalidated is a client-facing contract change, and strict:true and forced choices remain validated. The relaxation is described as matching OpenAI and vLLM behavior, and it is not itself a trust-boundary violation in the supplied evidence.

The local API exposes a relay with the pair key. Descriptions state that requests from other machines never use the paid network, and that local_token and cluster_local_token are used, with a 401 for other keys. The code enforcing this is not supplied. The changelog's later mentions of the pair's key being shown on the leading Mac are consistent with the existing local-token model.

No finding is raised because no code is visible. Implementation files were not provided, so the claims remain unverified.
